                    MOTION FOR LEAVE TO ANSWER AND ANSWER OF
                       PPL ELECTRIC UTILITIES CORPORATION


           Pursuant to Rules 212 and 213 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s

(“Commission”) Rules of Practice and Procedure, 1 PPL Electric Utilities Corporation (“PPL

Electric”) submits this answer (“Answer”) to the September 10, 2026 Motion for Leave to

Answer and Answer of PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”) in the above-captioned

proceeding. 2 PPL Electric files this Answer for the sole purpose of correcting a factual

mischaracterization of its Rate Schedule LP-6 that appears on page 92 of PJM’s Answer.


I.         MOTION FOR LEAVE TO ANSWER

           While an answer to an answer or protest is not a matter of right under the Commission’s

regulations, 3 the Commission routinely permits such answers when the answer provides useful

and relevant information that will assist the Commission in its decision-making process, 4

II.        ANSWER

           A.       PJM’s Characterization of PPL Electric’s Rate Schedule LP-6 is
                    Inaccurate and its use as Support for the Proposed LSE RBP Credit
                    Requirement is Misplaced.

           PJM’s Answer cites to the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission’s approval of PPL

Electric’s Rate Schedule LP-6 as support for PJM’s position that its proposed Load Serving

Entity (“LSE”) Reliability Backstop Procurement (“RBP”) credit requirements are reasonable,

and as evidence that LSEs in PJM are already requiring security from large loads to cover the

costs to serve those large loads. 8 While PPL Electric understands PJM’s intent in citing

examples of large load security practices, Rate Schedule LP-6 is not an appropriate

comparison, or an accurate example of such requirements being applied in this context.

           To clarify, Rate Schedule LP-6 governs infrastructure investment and minimum load

commitments associated with the delivery of retail electric service that PPL Electric provides




protest that “provided information that assisted us in our decision-making process”); Tallgrass Transmission,
LLC, 125 FERC ¶ 61,248, at P 26 (2008), reh’g denied, 150 FERC ¶ 61,224 (2015); PJM Interconnection,

                                                         2
 in its capacity as an Electric Distribution Company (“EDC”) in Pennsylvania, not in its role as

an LSE in Pennsylvania (a restructured state). Accordingly, Rate Schedule LP-6 does not

contain provisions that govern wholesale capacity procurement and generation supply to large

loads, nor does it relate to the buyer-side credit obligations that PJM’s RBP proposal would

impose on LSEs to cover the cost of capacity secured through the RBP.

       While it is true that PPL Electric is a designated LSE within PJM as a signatory to the

Reliability Assurance Agreement Among Load Serving Entities in the PJM Region (“RAA”), 9

and that PPL Electric is a provider of last resort under Pennsylvania’s Electricity Generation

Customer Choice and Competition Act, 66 Pa.C.S.A. § 2801, et seq, PPL Electric does not

currently serve as the LSE of record for any large load customers taking retail service pursuant

to Rate Schedule LP-6, nor does it anticipate that large load customers will seek to use provider

of last resort service to meet their capacity needs. Rate Schedule LP-6 does not relate to PPL

Electric’s role or obligations as an LSE and does not address the security or collateral that may

be required to be posted to satisfy RBP credit obligations that could be assigned to PPL Electric

in its distinct capacity as an LSE within PJM. Accordingly, PJM’s specific reliance on Rate

Schedule LP-6 for this proposition is misplaced and inaccurate and requires correction in the

record of this proceeding.
